EMERGENCY BRIDGE REPLACMENT The Briggs Emergency Bridge Replacement Project is located on a private property at 5425 Briggs Ranch Road, Healdsburg, California in Sonoma County within APN 132-170-022. The existing 96 inch rusty and collapsing culvert, surrounding fill and concrete abutment, and railcar are proposed to be replaced with a 70-foot-long railcar paired with drilled piers and concrete abutments. The streambanks will be graded and stabilized with riprap, willow-planted riprap and a boulder cluster as well as, erosion control fabric. Surfacing will include asphalt concrete (AC) paving along the new railcar and immediate approaches. New impervious areas (bridge and asphalt) include 1,644 square feet within the project area. The following trees are proposed for removal: (1) an 11 in. fir tree, (2) a 30 in. willow cluster, and (3) a 30 in. bay tree. All nearby trees within the grading area will have fencing installed extending around the dripline of the tree or as noted on the Civil Plan Set, Sheet C6. The estimated limits of disturbance include 6,769 sf or 0.16 acres. The grading summary includes an estimated 175.4 cubic yards of cut volume and 54.6 cubic yards of fill volume, resulting in a net cut volume (spoils) of 120.8 cubic yards. All spoils will be removed from the riparian area and permanently stored at a designated location on the project parcel. The project will be implemented during windows of time with no precipitation to complete individual tasks once permits are approved. If water is present, the dewatering plan (Civil Plan Set, Sheet C10) will be implemented. Project engineering is provided by Bauer Associates for geotechnical engineering, Geomorph Design Group for civil engineering, and MKM Associates for structural engineering. The project biologist is Swift Biological. The new railcar will be provided and installed by Daniel Steel and Machine. Additional construction contractors are to be determined. Project management is being provided by Pacific Watershed Associates.
